iter12 (2026-07-24): M1 slice 6 — CODE-FENCE ATTRIBUTES (PLAN.md §7 construct table line 279; backlog item (g) that iter10 found and deliberately deferred). Closes the last known SILENT DROP in the converter: FencedCodeBlockRenderer read only the first info-string token as the language and discarded every remaining token with no error, so ```cs title=Foo collapse linenumbers` published a plain code block and lost all three attributes. RESEARCHED BEFORE CODING via `gh api`, and the research overturned the spec's own example. THREE FINDINGS, each read from source rather than assumed: (1) mark's ACTUAL fence-attribute syntax is SPACE-SEPARATED, not `=`-separated — renderer/fencedcodeblock.go's reBlockDetails regex is `^(?:(\w*)|-)\s*\b(\S.*?\S?)??\s*(?:\btitle\s+(\S.*\S?))?$`, i.e. token[0] is the language (or `-` for none), the middle tokens are flag options, and `title` is a KEYWORD whose value is the REST OF THE LINE, unquoted. Confirmed against mark's own testdata/codes.md -> codes.html fixture pair: ```sh title A b c` yields <ac:parameter ac:name="title">A b c</ac:parameter>. So PLAN.md §7's `title=Foo` example is WRONG (flagged for Mirko in nextAction; PLAN.md deliberately NOT edited by the loop). ANSWERED the iter11 open question: a title with spaces is NOT quoted. (2) The exact emitted param ORDER, from mark's stdlib/stdlib.go ac:code template: language, collapse, theme, linenumbers, firstline, title, then <ac:plain-text-body>. (3) CRITICAL Markdig detail that the old code got wrong: with the DEFAULT info parser (FencedBlockParserBase.DefaultInfoParser, read at tag 1.3.2), FencedCodeBlock.Info holds ONLY the first token — the line is split at the first whitespace and the trimmed remainder goes to FencedCodeBlock.Arguments, which the old renderer never read. So the attributes were not merely mis-parsed, they were in a property nobody looked at. IMPLEMENTATION: ParseInfoLine rejoins Info + Arguments and scans it token by token (so the parse does not depend on where Markdig split), producing a private readonly record struct CodeFenceAttributes(Language, Collapse, LineNumbers, FirstLine, Title); Write emits the params in mark's order via a WriteParameter helper that XML-escapes the value as element content (the title is author text and can carry & < >). Supported attributes: collapse, nocollapse, linenumbers, a positive integer (Confluence's firstline, which also turns line numbering on, per mark's README table), and `title <rest of line>`. Keyword matching is case-insensitive (mark's is not) since widening what is understood can never silently misread a token. A repeated attribute takes its last value (`collapse nocollapse` -> not collapsed), matching mark's loop. An attribute in FIRST position means there is no language (```collapse` = collapse, no language), and `-` is mark's explicit no-language placeholder — both needed, since otherwise `​```collapse` would have parsed 'collapse' as an unknown language and then silently dropped the flag, reintroducing the very bug this slice fixes. THREE DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM MARK, all documented in the renderer's XML doc: (a) an UNRECOGNIZED attribute throws NotSupportedException, whereas mark treats any unknown token as a Confluence-Server `theme` name — mark's rule means a typo (`colapse`) or the `title=Foo` spelling silently becomes a bogus theme param, which destroys the fail-loud property entirely; WebFetch of Atlassian's Code Block macro doc confirmed the current Cloud macro documents only language/title/collapse/linenumbers/firstline and NO per-macro theme (theme is an admin-level default), so DocuMe emits exactly those five and guesses at nothing. (b) An absent param is OMITTED rather than written with its Confluence default; mark always writes collapse=false, which would be pure churn in every published body and in the approval hash (§8) for zero rendering difference — and would have forced a rewrite of the already-reviewed code-blocks golden. (c) `title` with no value throws instead of being ignored, and 0/negative firstline values throw (NumberStyles.None rejects the sign, so `-1` is an unknown attribute rather than a silently clamped one). The unknown-LANGUAGE path stays fail-safe on purpose (param omitted, never throws) and a test pins that asymmetry: an unmapped language costs only syntax highlighting, while a dropped attribute publishes a page the author did not ask for. 1 new golden case (17 total): code-fence-attributes, covering language+linenumbers+collapse+title, title-only, collapse-only, the no-language `-` form with firstline 12 plus a title carrying an & to pin escaping, and nocollapse being omitted.
